description: We are a team of aspiring innovators exploring the future of human space exploration through technology, creativity, and problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing LunarBase: Mission Control, an interactive educational simulator that challenges players to manage a lunar outpost and understand the complexities of sustaining human life on the Moon.
summary:
LunarBase — Mission Control is an interactive lunar survival simulator developed by Team SELENOVA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It places players in charge of a four-member astronaut crew living on the Moon for a 14-day mission. Players must manage essential resources—including oxygen, water, food, power, crew health, and radiation protection—while responding to unexpected mission events and making decisions that affect the crew's survival.

The project transforms the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth into an accessible, engaging learning experience. Through gameplay and educational explanations, users explore the importance of life-support systems, resource management, radiation awareness, and the complexities of future lunar exploration.
details:
The Problem

Living and working on the Moon presents major challenges. Astronauts must depend on limited supplies, reliable life-support systems, energy generation, and protection from the lunar environment. Understanding how these systems interact is essential to planning sustainable human missions.

Our Solution

LunarBase — Mission Control is an educational survival simulator that lets users experience some of these challenges through interactive decisions.

Key Features

  • Crew management: Lead a crew of four astronauts throughout a 14-day lunar mission.
  • Resource monitoring: Track oxygen, water, food, power, crew health, and radiation protection.
  • Mission events: Respond to unexpected situations such as equipment malfunctions, power shortages, and life-support disruptions.
  • Decision-making: Make daily choices that influence available resources and the crew's survival.
  • Educational experience: Learn why life-support, energy, resource conservation, and radiation protection matter in lunar exploration.

Intended Impact

The project aims to make lunar exploration more understandable and engaging, especially for students and young learners. It encourages systems thinking, problem-solving, and awareness of the challenges involved in establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon.

Technology and Development

The project was developed as an interactive web-based experience with AI-assisted development. Its resource values and survival mechanics are simplified game simulations for educational purposes, not actual NASA mission specifications.

Team

SELENOVA — Beyond Earth. Beyond Limits.

NASA's space-weather database provides information about space-weather events, including solar flares and coronal mass ejections. These events offer useful scientific context for understanding space-weather hazards relevant to human space exploration. Solar flare classifications should not be treated as direct measurements of astronaut radiation exposure.
Provides background on technologies being developed to support future lunar exploration and operations, helping inform the project's representation of lunar infrastructure and survival systems.
